Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Financial Group Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Apex Financial Group's results for the second quarter. With me this morning are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Risk Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Credit Officer; and David Kim, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Financial Group delivered excellent results in the second quarter, demonstrating the strength of our franchise and our ability to navigate a dynamic market environment.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Expanding our market share
2. Improving our efficiency ratio
3. Strengthening our balance sheet
4. Investing in our people
5. Driving innovation
6. Meeting our ESG goals.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our provision for credit losses, which came in at $1.2 billion amid disciplined reserving under CECL; our net interest margin expansion to 3.45% driven by asset yield improvements and funding cost management; robust fee income growth across wealth management, investment banking, and cards totaling $2.8 billion; strong loan portfolio expansion with commercial up nearly 10%, consumer at 6.5%, and mortgage at 3.1%; stable credit quality with NPLs at 0.82% and charge-offs at 0.38%; and controlled operating expenses at $2.48 billion reflecting efficiency gains.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. Apex Financial Group reported net income of $2.1 billion for the second quarter, or $1.62 per diluted share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 9% year-over-year due to higher asset yields from loan repricing and a stable deposit franchise. Non-interest income was up 14% driven by fee income momentum in wealth management, investment banking, and cards. Our efficiency ratio improved to 54.8%.

Let me start with our provision for credit losses, which totaled $1.2 billion this quarter. That's a 15% increase from $1.04 billion in the first quarter but down 8% from $1.3 billion a year ago. We continue to apply the CECL framework across our $850 billion loan portfolio, reserving for lifetime expected losses with forward-looking macro scenarios. Our multi-model approach pools loans by risk traits like FICO for consumers, PD grades for wholesale, and property types for CRE. We model PD using logistic regression enhanced by gradient-boosted trees on over 200 variables from internal payment data and external sources like Equifax. LGD draws from our $5 billion charge-off history, floored at 20% for secured consumer and 40% for unsecured, while EAD incorporates behavioral draws and prepayments linked to Treasury yields. Macro overlays include base, adverse, and severe scenarios, with this quarter's base assuming 2.1% GDP growth and Fed cuts. We added $150 million qualitative reserve for office CRE amid remote work trends, benchmarked against CoStar data.

Portfolio mix drove 45% of the provision from consumer at $540 million, up due to auto and card growth, while wholesale was 35% at $420 million, mainly CRE, and wealth lighter at $240 million. Net charge-offs improved to 0.42% annualized, delinquencies stabilized at 1.8%, with macro factors like higher rates on SOFR revolvers and regional strengths in the Southeast offsetting West Coast tech pressures. Our new CECL platform on AWS with XGBoost reduced volatility, and allowance is 2.18% of loans, providing strong coverage versus peers.

Turning to net interest margin, we achieved 3.45%, up 25 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 40 year-over-year, thanks to our asset-liability management in a volatile rate backdrop. Asset yields rose 62 basis points to 5.82%, led by C&I at 6.15% on $28 billion new commitments in tech and renewables, consumer at 4.95%, and securities at 4.20% with HTM dominance. Mortgage yields dipped slightly due to prepayment slowdowns, but ARMs position us for resets. Funding costs increased 37 basis points to 2.37%, with deposit betas at 45% below peers, sticky NIBDs at 28%, and wholesale via term notes at SOFR plus 85. Mix shifts favored higher-yield C&I and CRE at 42% of assets. ALM swaps hedged duration, and AI deposit pricing retained core funds. We expect further 10-15 basis point expansion.

Fee income hit $2.8 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, 28% of revenues, boosted by Client 360 cross-sell. Core growth was 11%. Wealth management led at $1.35 billion, up 16%, with AUM at $1.9 trillion on market gains and $28 billion NNM, strong in alternatives and APAC wealth transfer. Investment banking at $875 million, up 9%, shone in advisory on M&A, ECM IPOs, and DCM issuance. Cards at $575 million, up 20%, from $280 billion volumes on premium co-brands and blockchain payments. We guide to $11-11.5 billion for the year.

On loans, total held-for-investment grew 7.2% year-over-year to $28.4 billion, 2.1% sequentially. Commercial at 52% of portfolio surged 9.8% to $14.8 billion, C&I up 12.4% on capex, CRE 6.2% focused multifamily, led by Southeast logistics. Consumer at 28%, $7.9 billion, up 6.5% via auto at 10.2% and cross-sell. Mortgage at 20%, $5.7 billion, grew 3.1% on purchases despite refi weakness, with digital closings. This mix shift boosted yields and NIM.

Credit quality remains solid, with NPL ratio at 0.82%, down 12 basis points quarter-over-quarter, below industry at 1.10%; charge-offs at 0.38% annualized, under peers; delinquencies at 1.95%. Consumer strong, commercial stable with CRE restructurings, Southeast outperforming. GenAI early warnings and collections enhancements drive improvements. ACL at 1.28%, top-quartile metrics.

Operating expenses were $2.48 billion, up 4.2% year-over-year but flat sequentially, underlying 2.8% growth below peers. Compensation up 3.1% on tech hires, offset by offshoring; tech spend 12% on cloud and AI; other categories controlled. Efficiency at 54.8%, best in years. We target 3-4% full-year growth.

We are on track to achieve our financial targets for the year.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. From a risk perspective, we are closely monitoring commercial real estate exposure, particularly office, and interest rate volatility. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks, including de-risking non-core CRE sales, tighter underwriting overlays, and hedging duration gaps with swaps, to maintain a strong risk profile.

Lisa Patel:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains strong with non-performing loan ratio at 0.82% and net charge-offs at 0.38% annualized. We are actively managing our loan portfolio through restructurings, AI underwriting, and regional diversification, and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will be conducting a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the drivers and methodology behind the provision for credit losses this quarter?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, Mike. As I detailed, our $1.2 billion PCL reflects CECL methodology across the $850 billion portfolio, with pooled modeling for PD, LGD, and EAD enhanced by machine learning on 200 variables and macro scenarios assuming Fed cuts. Consumer drove 45% on auto and cards, wholesale 35% on CRE, with overlays for office valuations. Regional dynamics show Southeast strength and West Coast caution. Our new platform reduces volatility, allowance at 2.18% with 4.4x NCO coverage, better than peers. Q3 guide $1.1-1.3 billion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What is your strategy for sustaining net interest margin expansion?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Emily. NIM at 3.45% benefited from 62 bps asset yield lift on C&I repricing and $28 billion originations, low deposit betas at 45%, and mix to higher-yield commercial loans. Funding via notes and swaps hedged the curve; AI pricing retained deposits. Forward, 10-15 bps Q4 upside with cuts, plus private credit and embedded finance for yield boost.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
How are you addressing credit quality trends amid economic uncertainty?

Michael Chen:
David, thanks. We're monitoring CRE and rates closely, with sales of $2 billion office loans, LTV caps, and GenAI warnings flagging issues early. NPLs at 0.82%, NCOs 0.38%, delinquencies stable. Southeast outperforms, ACL covers stresses. Proactive like TDRs and syndication diversification keeps us resilient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim:
Can you update us on loan growth drivers by segment and fee income performance?

Lisa Patel:
Hi Sarah. Loans grew 7.2% YoY, commercial 9.8% on C&I capex and Southeast CRE, consumer 6.5% auto-led, mortgage 3.1% purchases. Disciplined underwriting via nCino AI. Fees at $2.8 billion: wealth $1.35B on NNM and AUM, IB $875M M&A/DCM, cards $575M volumes. Client 360 drives cross-sell.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your interest in Apex Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
